Case_19003/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Fig. 1: Right foot cutaneous lesion when it was first noticed (ie. three weeks before presenting to the emergency department)

description.short_caption: Right foot showing erythematous lesion with serpiginous border.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph depicts the dorsal aspect of the right foot. There is a well-demarcated, erythematous lesion with a serpiginous border, suggestive of a cutaneous process such as larva migrans. The surrounding skin appears mildly erythematous without overt swelling. The lesion is localized and does not appear to involve deeper structures.

Case_19003/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Fig. 2: Right foot cutaneous lesion two weeks after it was first noticed

description.short_caption: Right foot cutaneous lesion with blistering and erythema.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the dorsal aspect of the right foot with a prominent cutaneous lesion. The lesion includes a clear blister with surrounding erythema and mild swelling. The blister appears intact, and there is no visible purulence or crusting. The surrounding skin shows mild discoloration, suggesting inflammation or irritation.
visible_findings: clear blister on the dorsal right foot

Case_19003/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Fig. 3: Chest X-Ray at presentation. Patchy central opacities noted in the right and left lower lung zone.

description.short_caption: Chest X-ray showing patchy opacities in the lower lung zones bilaterally.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph demonstrating patchy opacities in the lower lung zones bilaterally, more prominent centrally. The heart and mediastinal contours appear normal, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The diaphragm and bony structures are intact. The findings are suggestive of a possible infectious or inflammatory process.
visible_findings: patchy opacities in bilateral lower lung zones

Case_19003/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Fig. 4: Chest X-Ray after treatment – changes resolved

description.short_caption: Chest X-ray showing resolution of prior abnormalities post-treatment.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph demonstrating clear lung fields with no visible consolidation, pleural effusion, or other abnormalities. The heart and mediastinal contours appear normal, and the diaphragm is well-defined bilaterally. The image suggests resolution of any prior pathological findings, consistent with post-treatment improvement.
